description: Every user-facing surface of the frontend, with the backend capability and contract behind it. This is the registry's vocabulary: a capability may only attach to a surface declared here. Status is honest: 'present' (implemented), 'partial' (implemented with declared 501 gaps), 'unsupported' (renders, backend not implemented).

surfaces.title: Sign-in, owner setup and session screens
surfaces.notes: Owned by the auth LEGO (P2). The frontend contract only consumes its envelopes and session rules.

surfaces.title: Application shell — header, main sidebar, settings sidebar, breadcrumbs
surfaces.notes: Entry visibility is scope- and flag-driven (P2 §10.3); the frontend must never hide a surface to fake capability.

surfaces.title: Home — workflow list/overview
surfaces.notes: Insights/data-table widgets on this surface are unimplemented backend capabilities and answer 501 (compatibility layer), never a fake empty payload.

surfaces.title: Settings pages (personal, users, API, security, usage, …)
surfaces.notes: P2 made the pages reachable and honest: reachable pages whose backend is not implemented answer 501 {code:'unsupported'} with owner/phase metadata.

surfaces.title: Workflow canvas (nodes, connections, panel)
surfaces.notes: The canvas is the reference surface for interaction contracts: save/run/execute-step must keep the P0-verified behavior.

surfaces.title: Node creator / node menu (palette, search, descriptions)
surfaces.notes: Community nodes / dynamic parameters behind this surface are unimplemented capabilities (501 with owner 'node-registry'/'dynamic-parameters'); the stock palette itself is complete (483 node types).

surfaces.title: Credentials list, credential editor and credential modal
surfaces.notes: OAuth1/OAuth2 flows and credential resolvers are unimplemented capabilities (501).

surfaces.title: Execution list, execution detail and execution errors
surfaces.notes: Error text from the engine arrives through the error model: code first, message as fallback (translation-ready).

surfaces.title: Webhook and form endpoints (triggers, test URLs, activation state)
surfaces.notes: Endpoint URLs are published in settings; trigger routing itself is tracked by the webhook/scheduler roadmap items and is not part of the frontend boundary.

surfaces.title: Toasts, banners, push-driven updates and system messages
surfaces.notes: Push event names and payload keys are contract data (contract.mjs EVENTS); the frontend never invents its own channel.

surfaces.title: Modals and overlays (workflow settings, credential modal, confirmations)
surfaces.notes: Frontend-owned surface: dialogs carry no backend capability of their own, they render data whose capability belongs to another surface.

surfaces.title: Error presentation — page-level errors, toasts, node/execution errors, unsupported capability notices
surfaces.notes: The single place where a backend error code becomes a displayable message; today the fallback text, later the localized one.

surfaces.title: Workflow canvas — nodes, edges, viewport and selection
surfaces.notes: P2-S14 Layer 3 strangler slice (issue #240): composite region of the workflow editor delivered as its own pilot. The graph model is handed over to the frontend-lego canvas surface; the frontend never fetches a graph, performs no engine call and never mutates the workflow document.

surfaces.title: Node parameter / NDV panel (one node type's parameters)
surfaces.notes: P2-S15 Layer 3 strangler slice (issue #240): the parameter panel that edits one node type's parameters through the parameter contract. Definitions and values are handed over; expression evaluation stays behind the declared boundary - the frontend never evaluates and never posts the workflow.
